facts.claim: IBM MQ dev image default objects and credentials (queues, channels, users).
facts.value: Default dev objects (created when MQ_DEV != false): queues DEV.QUEUE.1, DEV.QUEUE.2, DEV.QUEUE.3, and DEV.DEAD.LETTER.QUEUE (set as the QM dead-letter queue). Channels: DEV.ADMIN.SVRCONN (admin user only) and DEV.APP.SVRCONN (app user only, no admin). Users: admin (administration) and app (messaging, in group mqclient). Default queue manager name example: QM1 (via MQ_QMGR_NAME).
facts.source_quote: 'DEV.QUEUE.1 / DEV.QUEUE.2 / DEV.QUEUE.3 / DEV.DEAD.LETTER.QUEUE - configured as the Queue Manager's Dead Letter Queue.' ... 'DEV.ADMIN.SVRCONN - configured to only allow the admin user to connect' ... 'DEV.APP.SVRCONN - does not allow administrative users to connect. Only the app user can connect.' ... 'User admin for administration ... User app for messaging (in a group called mqclient)'.
facts.notes: IMPORTANT credential change: from IBM MQ v9.4.0.0 the env vars MQ_ADMIN_PASSWORD / MQ_APP_PASSWORD are DEPRECATED; passwords for admin and app MUST be set via container secrets (mqAdminPassword / mqAppPassword). There is no fixed built-in default password; the doc examples use 'passw0rd' (min 8 chars). The admin/app users are only created if their password (secret) is set. Web console on port 9443 (/ibmmq/console), listener on 1414.

facts.claim: How Exception report feedback codes are determined.
facts.value: Exception report messages do NOT use a fixed MQFB_* value; the MQMD Feedback field is set to an IBM MQ reason code (an MQRC_* value, e.g. MQRC_PUT_INHIBITED, MQRC_Q_FULL, MQRC_NOT_AUTHORIZED) describing why the message could not be delivered.
facts.source_quote: For exception report messages, Feedback contains an IBM MQ reason code [such as MQRC_PUT_INHIBITED, MQRC_Q_FULL, MQRC_NOT_AUTHORIZED]. The range MQFB_SYSTEM_FIRST..MQFB_SYSTEM_LAST includes the general MQFB_* codes and the MQRC_* reason codes that can occur when the message cannot be put on the destination queue.
facts.notes: IBM Feedback (MQLONG) page via mirror (ibm.com 403). Ranges confirmed in 9.4.5.0 bytecode: MQFB_SYSTEM_FIRST=1, MQFB_SYSTEM_LAST=65535, MQFB_APPL_FIRST=65536, MQFB_APPL_LAST=999999999. So an Exception report's feedback is read as the reason code, not a single 'MQFB_EXCEPTION' constant (which does not exist).

facts.claim: When a report is requested without an explicit msg-id/correl-id option, MQRO_COPY_MSG_ID_TO_CORREL_ID is assumed (original MessageId -> report CorrelationId).
facts.value: TRUE. MQRO_COPY_MSG_ID_TO_CORREL_ID (value 0) is the default action: the original message's MsgId is copied to the CorrelId of the report/reply message. (For the report's own MsgId, MQRO_NEW_MSG_ID is the default = a new MsgId is generated.)
facts.source_quote: MQRO_COPY_MSG_ID_TO_CORREL_ID: This is the default action, and indicates that if a report or reply is generated as a result of this message, the MsgId of this message is copied to the CorrelId of the report or reply message.
facts.notes: IBM Report (MQLONG) page via mirror (ibm.com 403). Value 0 confirmed in 9.4.5.0 bytecode. Note the two independent id options: CorrelId default = COPY_MSG_ID_TO_CORREL_ID; report's MsgId default = NEW_MSG_ID ('If this option is not specified, MQRO_NEW_MSG_ID is assumed.'). Both are value 0 / the assumed defaults.

facts.claim: COA is generated when the message ARRIVES on the destination queue.
facts.value: TRUE. A COA report is generated by the queue manager that owns the destination queue when the message is placed on the destination queue.
facts.source_quote: MQRO_COA ... This type of report is generated by the queue manager that owns the destination queue when the message is placed on the destination queue.
facts.notes: IBM Report (MQLONG) page via mirror (ibm.com 403). Version-stable across MQ 9.x.

facts.claim: COD is generated when the message is RETRIEVED/consumed.
facts.value: TRUE. A COD report is generated by the queue manager when an application retrieves the message from the destination queue in a way that deletes the message from the queue (a destructive MQGET).
facts.source_quote: MQRO_COD ... This type of report is generated by the queue manager when an application retrieves the message from the destination queue in a way that deletes the message from the queue.
facts.notes: IBM Report (MQLONG) page via mirror. A COD is NOT generated if the message Format is MQFMT_DEAD_LETTER_HEADER (i.e. it went to the DLQ), and MQRO_COD is not valid for an XCF destination queue.

facts.claim: Under syncpoint the message is not visible (COA does not flow / report not retrievable) until the producer COMMITS.
facts.value: TRUE. If the message is put as part of a unit of work, the COA report message generated by the queue manager can be retrieved only if (after) the unit of work is committed. For COD, the report is generated within the consumer's unit of work and is not available until that unit of work commits; if it is backed out, the report is not sent.
facts.source_quote: If the message is put as part of a unit of work, and the destination queue is a local queue, the COA report message generated by the queue manager can be retrieved only if the unit of work is committed. ... If the message is retrieved as part of a unit of work, the report message is generated within the same unit of work, so that the report is not available until the unit of work is committed. If the unit of work is backed out, the report is not sent.
facts.notes: IBM Report (MQLONG) page via mirror (ibm.com 403). Confirms the producer-commit gating for COA and consumer-commit gating for COD.

facts.claim: Default persistence of a generated report relative to the original: can a report be non-persistent even if the original is persistent, or does it inherit persistence?
facts.value: REFUTED as stated. A generated report message INHERITS the original message's persistence by default ('Copied from the original message descriptor'). Therefore a persistent original yields a persistent report by default; the report is NOT non-persistent when the original is persistent. (Applies uniformly to COA, COD, exception, expiration, PAN, NAN reports per the IBM 'Contents of the message descriptor for a report message' table.)
facts.source_quote: Contents of the message descriptor for a report message — Persistence: Copied from the original message descriptor.
facts.notes: IBM Report (MQLONG) page via mirror (ibm.com 403). LOAD-BEARING: the IBM table lists Persistence as 'Copied from the original message descriptor' with no COA/COD carve-out, so the common belief that COA/COD reports are non-persistent by default is incorrect for IBM MQ. (Behaviour can be altered separately via the destination/queue or PUT options, but the DEFAULT for a queue-manager-generated report is to inherit the original's persistence.) Confusion likely stems from activity/trace-route reports, which are a separate mechanism.

facts.claim: How keystore/truststore are supplied to IBM MQ classes for JMS for TLS (javax.net.ssl.* system properties vs sslSocketFactory).

TLS is only active if a CipherSuite is set.
facts.source_quote: "...want to: ... Change the keystore and truststore in use. ... create a javax.net.ssl.SSLSocketFactory object ... use the MQConnectionFactory.setSSLSocketFactory() method to configure JMS to use the customized SSLSocketFactory object. ... If this property is not set, the default SSLSocketFactory object is used."  (plus permission entries javax.net.ssl.keyStore / javax.net.ssl.keyStorePassword)
facts.notes: develop.pdf 'Supplying a customized SSLSocketFactory'. Default path relies on JVM JSSE settings (javax.net.ssl.keyStore/trustStore). Note: after setSSLSocketFactory() the MQConnectionFactory can no longer be bound into JNDI. From IBM MQ 9.4.5 you can also supply a custom SSLSocketFactory specifically for JWT/HTTPS token retrieval (WMQ_SSL_SOCKET_FACTORY field = XMSC_WMQ_SSL_SOCKET_FACTORY).

facts.claim: A concrete TLS 1.2 CipherSpec (QMgr/MQSC) <-> CipherSuite (Java) pair.
facts.value: CipherSpec ECDHE_RSA_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (set on the SVRCONN channel) maps to CipherSuite SSL_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (IBM JRE) / TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (Oracle JRE), protocol TLS 1.2, FIPS 140-2 and 140-3 compatible. (256-bit variant: CipherSpec ECDHE_RSA_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 -> SSL_/TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384.)
facts.source_quote: ECDHE_RSA_AES_128_GCM_SHA256  SSL_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256  TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256  TLS 1.2 Yes Yes
facts.notes: From Table 41 'CipherSpecs supported by IBM MQ and their equivalent CipherSuites' (IBM JRE vs Oracle JRE columns). The IBM JRE CipherSuite uses an SSL_ prefix while Oracle/standard uses TLS_ for TLS 1.2 names - this naming divergence is the historical reason for the useIBMCipherMappings property.

facts.claim: A concrete TLS 1.3 CipherSpec <-> CipherSuite pair.
facts.value: For TLS 1.3 the CipherSpec and the CipherSuite have the SAME name in both JREs, e.g. CipherSpec TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 = CipherSuite TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 (also TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384). Protocol TLS 1.3; FIPS 140-3 compatible.
facts.source_quote: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256  TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256  TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256  TLS 1.3 No Yes   /   TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 ... TLS 1.3 No Yes
facts.notes: Same Table 41. TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 are enabled by default for TLS 1.3; TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 is supported but not enabled by default. Generic specs ANY_TLS13, ANY_TLS12, ANY_TLS12_OR_HIGHER, ANY_TLS13_OR_HIGHER also exist.

From 9.4.0 a Cipher can be defined as either the CipherSpec or the CipherSuite name and is handled correctly automatically. (In earlier MQ versions the property controlled which mapping table - IBM SSL_ vs Oracle TLS_ - was used.)
facts.source_quote: "From IBM MQ 9.4.0, a Cipher can be defined as either the CipherSpec or CipherSuite name and is handled correctly by IBM MQ. Note: The Java System Property com.ibm.mq.cfg.useIBMCipherMappings, which controlled which mappings were used in earlier versions of IBM MQ, is no longer needed and is removed from the product at IBM MQ 9.4.0."

facts.claim: AUTHINFO IDPWOS CONNAUTH CHCKCLNT keyword and its allowed values for client password checking.
facts.value: Keyword CHCKCLNT on AUTHINFO TYPE(IDPWOS) (and IDPWLDAP). Values: NONE (credentials ignored), OPTIONAL (checked only if supplied), REQUIRED (all client apps must supply valid user+password), REQDADM (privileged user IDs must supply credentials; non-privileged treated as OPTIONAL).
facts.source_quote: "CHCKCLNT ... valid only for an AUTHTYPE of IDPWOS or IDPWLDAP. ... NONE ... OPTIONAL ... REQUIRED All client applications must provide authentication credentials in the MQCSP structure. ... REQDADM All client applications using a privileged user ID must provide authentication credentials..."  Syntax: CHCKCLNT(NONE)/CHCKCLNT(OPTIONAL)/CHCKCLNT(REQUIRED)/CHCKCLNT(REQDADM)
facts.notes: To require user/password from clients: DEFINE/ALTER AUTHINFO(...) AUTHTYPE(IDPWOS) CHCKCLNT(REQUIRED) ADOPTCTX(YES), then ALTER QMGR CONNAUTH(<authinfo-name>) and REFRESH SECURITY TYPE(CONNAUTH). The QMGR CONNAUTH CHCKCLNT is the default; a matching CHLAUTH rule's CHCKCLNT can override it (or use ASQMGR to defer to the QMGR setting). REQDADM not valid on z/OS.

facts.claim: MQSC keyword spellings for CHLAUTH: command, TYPE values, USERSRC values, block/allow/require-user mappings.
facts.value: Command: SET CHLAUTH(channel-profile-name) TYPE(...) ACTION(ADD|REPLACE|REMOVE|REMOVEALL). TYPE values: BLOCKUSER, BLOCKADDR, SSLPEERMAP, ADDRESSMAP, USERMAP, QMGRMAP. Mapping rules use USERSRC(MAP|NOACCESS|CHANNEL) and MCAUSER(user). Block a user/admins: TYPE(BLOCKUSER) USERLIST(name | *MQADMIN). Block IPs: TYPE(BLOCKADDR) ADDRLIST(...). Allow/map a user: TYPE(USERMAP) CLNTUSER(client-user) USERSRC(MAP) MCAUSER(user). Per-rule client checking: CHCKCLNT(ASQMGR|REQUIRED|REQDADM).
facts.source_quote: "SET CHLAUTH ( channel-profile-name ) ... TYPE ... (BLOCKUSER) USERLIST(...) (BLOCKADDR) ADDRLIST(...) (SSLPEERMAP) (ADDRESSMAP) (USERMAP) CLNTUSER(...) CHCKCLNT(ASQMGR|REQDADM|REQUIRED) (QMGRMAP) QMNAME(...) USERSRC(MAP) MCAUSER(...) USERSRC(NOACCESS) USERSRC(CHANNEL) ADDRESS(...)"
facts.notes: Canonical MQSC verb is SET CHLAUTH (there is no separate DEFINE CHLAUTH; use SET/REMOVE via ACTION). USERMAP rules apply only to SVRCONN channels. *MQADMIN in a USERLIST = privileged/admin users (on Linux/AIX = mqm group members). Queue-manager attribute CHLAUTH(DISABLED|ENABLED) gates whether rules are enforced: 'This attribute specifies whether the rules defined by channel authentication records are used.'

facts.claim: IBM MQ blocks remote administrative (privileged) access by default via default CHLAUTH records on a newly created queue manager.
facts.value: Strongly supported but no clean verbatim primary-source quote could be captured (the IBM Documentation/Support pages that state this are JavaScript-rendered and could not be fetched as text). The MECHANISM is confirmed: CHLAUTH(ENABLED) enforces rules, and default rules use USERSRC(NOACCESS) plus BLOCKUSER('*MQADMIN') to block privileged users on SYSTEM.* / SYSTEM.ADMIN.SVRCONN channels.
facts.source_quote: (IBM Support page title) 'MQ RC 2035 MQRC_NOT_AUTHORIZED ... when using client connection as an MQ Administrator (CHLAUTH, channel authentication records)' - page body is JS-rendered and not extractable as verbatim text.
facts.notes: Honest gap: the well-known 'remote admins blocked by default since MQ 7.1' behavior is confirmed at the mechanism level from mq94.refadmin.pdf (CHLAUTH attribute meaning, *MQADMIN, USERSRC(NOACCESS)), but I could not fetch a verbatim 'blocked by default' sentence from a primary IBM page. To allow a remote admin: add a CHLAUTH USERMAP/ADDRESSMAP rule with USERSRC(MAP) MCAUSER(...), or set ALTER QMGR CHLAUTH(DISABLED) (not recommended for production).

## Impact on the brief's premises

**P2 — `allclient 9.4.5.0` / Java 21:** NO CONTRADICTION. Both valid: `com.ibm.mq.allclient:9.4.5.0` is a real artifact (javax.jms, JMS 2.0), and Java 21 is supported on 9.4.x (Semeru 21 bundled). Caveats: 9.4.5.1 is the newest fixpack (9.4.5.0 resolves normally); the corresponding image tag is `9.4.5.0-r1/r2`, not bare `9.4.5.0`.

**P6 — Report constants / default COPY_MSG_ID / persistence:** PARTIALLY CONTRADICTED.
- Default `MQRO_COPY_MSG_ID_TO_CORREL_ID`: **CONFIRMED** (value 0, the assumed one).
- Persistence: **REFUTED** — reports **inherit** the persistence of the original; persistent original → persistent report. The belief that COA/COD are non-persistent by default is wrong.
- The "MQRO_* values from WMQConstants" framing: **CORRECTED** — MQRO_*/MQFB_* live in `com.ibm.mq.constants.CMQC`/`MQConstants`, not in `WMQConstants`.

**P10 — `pooled-jms` javax version:** NOT CONTRADICTED, but SUBOPTIMAL. "1.x = javax.jms" is correct, but **2.x is also javax** (latest 2.0.9) and is the maintained javax line recommended for a new project. Pinning 1.x leaves you on an older series, not a wrong one. (3.x = jakarta.jms.)

**Corretto 25 runtime (JDK certification / Security Manager):** VIABLE with caveats, and two of the brief's assumptions are REFUTED.
- "Java 25 not listed for 9.4.5": **REFUTED** — there is dedicated operational guidance in the 9.4.x docs.
- "allclient breaks on JDK 24/25 due to SecurityManager (JEP 486)": **REFUTED** — the SecurityManager is optional and not enabled by the samples/scripts.
- Real actions when running on Corretto 25: pass `--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED` (native-access warning in `System.loadLibrary`) and **avoid TLS_RSA_* CipherSpecs** (disabled as of Java 25).
- The "8/11/17/21 certified" enumeration remains **not confirmable** by a primary source (SPCR report JS-rendered) — do not assert it as a hard fact.
